static_contents.reading: Each qword decomposes into two plausible 32-bit RVAs: a small .text RVA in the low half and a .rdata RVA in the high half. The region therefore reads like a table of 32-bit pairs rather than a block of pointer-sized singletons.

searches_exhausted: direct RIP-relative qword store in Engine.dll: 0
direct RIP-relative qword store in Game.dll: 0 (a cross-module store would use a computed base, so this scan cannot exclude it)
LEA of the slot address in Engine.dll: 0
LEA of a neighbouring base followed by a store at the matching offset: 0
the literal 0x421428 as an immediate in Engine.dll, Game.dll and Direct3D11.dll: 0
relocation entries covering 0x421400..0x421460: 0, so the static contents are not loader-applied pointers
what_is_excluded: The slot is not published by any direct store in Engine.dll, not by a constant-offset store in any of the three modules, and not by a loader relocation.

hard_boundary.fact: Determining who writes the slot at runtime requires a memory-write watchpoint.
hard_boundary.prohibition: The project forbids debuggers after the 2026-11-04 breakpoint attempt terminated the client with 0x80000003.
hard_boundary.consequence: Static analysis alone cannot currently answer the question, and I will not guess an answer or substitute a hand-made engine object.
